column1: # kind|MM-DD|year|Greek name|English name|English biography   (English versions of the short biographies in data/bios; kind is always bio)

bio|05-03|1902|Αλφρέντ Καστλέρ|Alfred Kastler|Alfred Kastler was born in Alsace and was a French physicist. He developed the method of optical pumping, which makes it possible to study the energy levels of atoms, and in 1966 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics.

bio|05-03|1961|Μωρίς Μερλώ-Ποντύ|Maurice Merleau-Ponty|Maurice Merleau-Ponty was a French philosopher of phenomenology. In his work "Phenomenology of Perception" he emphasised the role of the body in experience. He taught at the Collège de France and was a friend of Sartre.

bio|05-03|1977|Μαριάμ Μιρζαχανί|Maryam Mirzakhani|Maryam Mirzakhani was born in Tehran and was a mathematician. She researched the geometry of Riemann surfaces. In 2014 she became the first woman to win the Fields Medal. She died young, in 2017, at the age of 40.

bio|05-03|1987|Δαλιδά|Dalida|Dalida was born in Egypt to an Italian family and became a great singer in France. She sang hits such as "Gigi l'amoroso" and "Paroles, paroles" and was also an actress. She took her own life in 1987.

bio|05-04|1825|Τόμας Χάξλεϋ|Thomas Huxley|Thomas Huxley was an English biologist. He zealously defended Darwin's theory of evolution and earned the nickname "Darwin's bulldog". He also introduced the term "agnosticism".

bio|05-04|1881|Αλέξανδρος Κερένσκι|Alexander Kerensky|Alexander Kerensky was a Russian politician. He headed the Provisional Government in 1917, until it was overthrown by the Bolsheviks in the October Revolution. He lived in exile in the United States.

bio|05-04|1928|Χόσνι Μουμπάρακ|Hosni Mubarak|Hosni Mubarak was an Egyptian pilot and politician. He was president of Egypt from 1981 to 2011, when he resigned after the popular uprising of the Arab Spring. He was later put on trial and died in 2020.

bio|05-04|1929|Ώντρεϊ Χέπμπορν|Audrey Hepburn|Audrey Hepburn was born in Brussels and became a Hollywood actress. She won an Oscar for "Roman Holiday" and became known also for "Breakfast at Tiffany's". Later she became a UNICEF Goodwill Ambassador.

bio|05-04|1938|Καρλ φον Οσιέτσκι|Carl von Ossietzky|Carl von Ossietzky was a German journalist and pacifist. He revealed Germany's secret rearmament and was imprisoned by the Nazis. In 1935 he was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize, and he died in 1938.

bio|05-04|1980|Γιόσιπ Μπροζ Τίτο|Josip Broz Tito|Josip Broz Tito was the leader of Yugoslavia from 1945 until his death. He led the partisans in the Second World War and, as the founder of the Non-Aligned Movement, pursued an independent policy from the Soviet Union.

bio|05-04|1987|Σεσκ Φάμπρεγας|Cesc Fàbregas|Cesc Fàbregas is a Spanish footballer. He played as a midfielder for Barcelona, Arsenal and Chelsea, and he won the 2010 World Cup and two European Championships with Spain.

bio|05-04|2013|Κριστιάν ντε Ντυβ|Christian de Duve|Christian de Duve was a Belgian biochemist. He discovered lysosomes and peroxisomes in cells and in 1974 shared the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.

bio|05-05|1705|Λεοπόλδος Α΄|Leopold I|Leopold I was emperor of the Holy Roman Empire from 1658. During his reign the Habsburgs repelled the siege of Vienna in 1683 and then took Hungary from the Ottomans.

bio|05-05|1813|Σαίρεν Κίρκεγκωρ|Søren Kierkegaard|Søren Kierkegaard was a Danish philosopher and theologian. He is considered the father of existentialism. He wrote "Fear and Trembling" and "Either/Or" and emphasised individual faith and responsibility.

bio|05-05|1818|Καρλ Μαρξ|Karl Marx|Karl Marx was born in Trier and was a German philosopher, economist and revolutionary. With Engels he wrote "The Communist Manifesto", and on his own he wrote "Capital". His ideas influenced the labour movement.

bio|05-05|1821|Ναπολέων Α΄|Napoleon I|Napoleon I died on 5 May 1821 on Saint Helena, where he had been exiled by the British after the Battle of Waterloo. He was a general of the French Revolution and Emperor of the French.

bio|05-05|1846|Χένρικ Σιενκιέβιτς|Henryk Sienkiewicz|Henryk Sienkiewicz was a Polish writer. He wrote the historical novel "Quo Vadis", set in the time of Nero. In 1905 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|05-05|1977|Λούντβιγκ Έρχαρντ|Ludwig Erhard|Ludwig Erhard was a German economist and politician. As minister of economics he was the originator of the "economic miracle" of West Germany, and in 1963 he became chancellor. He died in 1977.
bio|05-05|1983|Χένρι Κάβιλ|Henry Cavill|Henry Cavill is an English actor. He became known as Superman in the films "Man of Steel" and as Geralt in the series "The Witcher".

bio|05-05|1988|Αντέλ|Adele|Adele is an English singer and songwriter. She became famous with the albums "19", "21" and "25" and with songs such as "Rolling in the Deep" and "Hello". She has won many Grammy Awards.

bio|05-05|1995|Μιχαήλ Μποτβίνικ|Mikhail Botvinnik|Mikhail Botvinnik was a Soviet chess player. He was world chess champion three times and the teacher of Karpov, Kasparov and Kramnik. He was also a mechanical engineer.

bio|05-06|1758|Μαξιμιλιανός Ροβεσπιέρος|Maximilien Robespierre|Maximilien Robespierre was a French politician of the French Revolution. He was a leading member of the Jacobins and of the Committee of Public Safety, and he was associated with the Reign of Terror. He was executed in 1794.

bio|05-06|1856|Σίγκμουντ Φρόιντ|Sigmund Freud|Sigmund Freud was born in Moravia and lived in Vienna. He was a neurologist and founder of psychoanalysis. He wrote "The Interpretation of Dreams" and developed concepts such as the unconscious and the Oedipus complex. He died in London in 1939.

bio|05-06|1859|Αλεξάντερ φον Χούμπολτ|Alexander von Humboldt|Alexander von Humboldt was a German naturalist and explorer. He travelled in Latin America and wrote "Cosmos", a work on nature. He is regarded as a pioneer of geography and ecology.

bio|05-06|1862|Χένρι Ντέιβιντ Θόρω|Henry David Thoreau|Henry David Thoreau was an American writer and philosopher. He wrote "Walden", about his life in a hut near Walden Pond, and the essay "Civil Disobedience".

bio|05-06|1915|Όρσον Γουέλς|Orson Welles|Orson Welles was an American director and actor. He directed and starred in the film "Citizen Kane" in 1941, which is considered one of the most important films in the history of cinema.

bio|05-06|1949|Μορίς Μαίτερλινκ|Maurice Maeterlinck|Maurice Maeterlinck was a Belgian writer. He wrote the symbolist play "The Blue Bird" and "Pelléas and Mélisande". In 1911 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|05-06|1953|Τόνι Μπλερ|Tony Blair|Tony Blair is a British Labour Party politician. He was Prime Minister of the United Kingdom from 1997 to 2007. He supported the invasion of Iraq in 2003, which caused great controversy.

bio|05-06|1961|Τζορτζ Κλούνεϊ|George Clooney|George Clooney is an American actor and director. He became known for the series "ER" and the films "Ocean's Eleven" and "Syriana", for which he won the Oscar for Best Supporting Actor.

bio|05-06|1992|Μαρλέν Ντίτριχ|Marlene Dietrich|Marlene Dietrich was a German-American actress and singer. She became famous with the film "The Blue Angel" in 1930 and became a symbol of Hollywood glamour. She opposed the Nazis.

bio|05-07|973|Όθων Α΄|Otto I|Otto I the Great was king of Germany and in 962 was crowned emperor of the Holy Roman Empire by the pope. He defeated the Hungarians at the Battle of Lechfeld in 955 and strengthened the state.

bio|05-07|1711|Ντέιβιντ Χιουμ|David Hume|David Hume was a Scottish philosopher and historian. He wrote the "Treatise of Human Nature" and supported empiricism and scepticism. He influenced Kant and many others.

bio|05-07|1825|Αντόνιο Σαλιέρι|Antonio Salieri|Antonio Salieri was an Italian composer and conductor at the court in Vienna. He taught Beethoven and Schubert. The myth of his rivalry with Mozart began after his death.

bio|05-07|1833|Γιοχάνες Μπραμς|Johannes Brahms|Johannes Brahms was born in Hamburg and was a composer of the Romantic era. He wrote four symphonies, the "German Requiem" and the "Hungarian Dances". He lived in Vienna.

bio|05-07|1840|Πιότρ Ίλιτς Τσαϊκόφσκι|Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky|Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky was a Russian composer of the Romantic era. He wrote the ballets "Swan Lake", "The Sleeping Beauty" and "The Nutcracker", as well as symphonies and the "1812 Overture".

bio|05-07|1840|Κάσπαρ Ντάβιντ Φρίντριχ|Caspar David Friedrich|Caspar David Friedrich was a German painter of the Romantic movement. He became known for his landscapes with solitary figures and mist, such as "Wanderer above the Sea of Fog".

bio|05-07|1861|Ραμπιντρανάθ Ταγκόρ|Rabindranath Tagore|Rabindranath Tagore was an Indian poet, writer and composer from Bengal. He wrote the collection "Gitanjali" and the lyrics of the national anthems of India and Bangladesh. In 1913 he became the first non-European to be awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|05-07|1867|Βλαντυσλάβ Ρέυμοντ|Władysław Reymont|Władysław Reymont was a Polish writer. He wrote the novel "The Peasants", which describes life in the Polish countryside. In 1924 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|05-07|1892|Γιόσιπ Μπροζ Τίτο|Josip Broz Tito|Josip Broz Tito was born in Croatia. He led the partisans in the Second World War and governed Yugoslavia from 1945 to 1980. He was a founder of the Non-Aligned Movement.

bio|05-07|1941|Τζέιμς Φρέιζερ|James Frazer|James Frazer was a Scottish anthropologist. He wrote the multi-volume work "The Golden Bough", a comparative study of mythology and religion, which influenced many writers.

bio|05-08|1737|Έντουαρντ Γκίμπον|Edward Gibbon|Edward Gibbon was an English historian and Member of Parliament. He wrote "The History of the Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire", published from 1776 to 1789, which is a classic of historiography.

bio|05-08|1794|Αντουάν Λωράν Λαβουαζιέ|Antoine Lavoisier|Antoine Lavoisier was a French chemist. He is regarded as the father of modern chemistry: he discovered the role of oxygen in combustion and formulated the law of conservation of mass. He was beheaded in 1794 during the French Revolution.

bio|05-08|1828|Ανρί Ντυνάν|Henry Dunant|Henry Dunant was born in Geneva. After seeing the victims of the Battle of Solferino in 1859, he proposed the creation of an organisation to care for the wounded, which led to the founding of the Red Cross. In 1901 he was awarded the first Nobel Peace Prize.

bio|05-08|1873|Τζον Στιούαρτ Μιλ|John Stuart Mill|John Stuart Mill was a British philosopher and economist. He wrote "On Liberty", "Utilitarianism" and "The Subjection of Women". He was a champion of individual liberty and of women's rights.

bio|05-08|1880|Γκυστάβ Φλωμπέρ|Gustave Flaubert|Gustave Flaubert was a French writer. He wrote the novel "Madame Bovary", which became a landmark of realism, and "Sentimental Education". He was particularly careful about his style.

bio|05-08|1884|Χάρυ Τρούμαν|Harry Truman|Harry Truman was the 33rd president of the United States, from 1945 to 1953. He ordered the atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki, announced the "Truman Doctrine" and supported the Marshall Plan.

bio|05-08|1899|Φρίντριχ Χάγιεκ|Friedrich Hayek|Friedrich Hayek was born in Vienna and became an economist and philosopher. He wrote "The Road to Serfdom" and supported liberal economics. In 1974 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Economics.

bio|05-08|1903|Πωλ Γκωγκέν|Paul Gauguin|Paul Gauguin was a French painter of post-Impressionism and Symbolism. He left Europe and lived in Tahiti, where he painted exotic works in vivid colours. He died in the Marquesas Islands in 1903.
bio|05-08|1975|Ενρίκε Ιγκλέσιας|Enrique Iglesias|Enrique Iglesias is a Spanish singer and the son of Julio Iglesias. He has sold tens of millions of records with hits such as "Hero" and "Bailamos".

bio|05-09|1805|Φρίντριχ Σίλερ|Friedrich Schiller|Friedrich Schiller was a German poet, playwright and historian. He wrote the plays "The Robbers", "Wallenstein" and "William Tell", and the poem "Ode to Joy", which Beethoven set to music.
bio|05-09|1860|Τζ. Μ. Μπάρι|J. M. Barrie|J. M. Barrie was a Scottish writer and playwright. He created "Peter Pan", the boy who never grows up, first as a play in 1904 and then as a novel.

bio|05-09|1883|Χοσέ Ορτέγα ι Γκασέτ|José Ortega y Gasset|José Ortega y Gasset was a Spanish philosopher. He wrote "The Revolt of the Masses" and supported "perspectivism". He was an important thinker of 20th-century Spain.

bio|05-09|1921|Σόφι Σολ|Sophie Scholl|Sophie Scholl was a German student and a member of the "White Rose" resistance group against the Nazis. She was arrested together with her brother Hans in 1943 for distributing leaflets and was executed at the age of 21.

bio|05-09|1931|Άλμπερτ Αβραάμ Μάικελσον|Albert Abraham Michelson|Albert Michelson was born in Poland and was an American physicist. Together with Morley he carried out the Michelson-Morley experiment, which did not detect the "aether". In 1907 he became the first American to win the Nobel Prize in Physics.

bio|05-09|1936|Γκλέντα Τζάκσον|Glenda Jackson|Glenda Jackson was an English actress and politician. She won two Academy Awards for Best Actress and was a Labour Member of Parliament from 1992 to 2015. She died in 2023.
bio|05-09|1959|Γιάνος Άντερ|János Áder|János Áder is a Hungarian politician and lawyer. From 2012 to 2022 he was president of Hungary.
bio|05-09|1978|Άλντο Μόρο|Aldo Moro|Aldo Moro was an Italian Christian Democrat politician and prime minister. He was kidnapped by the Red Brigades in March 1978 and was found dead on 9 May 1978.

bio|05-09|1986|Τένσινγκ Νοργκέι|Tenzing Norgay|Tenzing Norgay was a Sherpa and mountaineer. On 29 May 1953, together with Edmund Hillary, he became one of the first people to reach the summit of Mount Everest. He died in 1986.

bio|05-10|238|Μαξιμίνος Θραξ|Maximinus Thrax|Maximinus Thrax was a Roman emperor from 235 to 238. He was the first emperor to come from the army, without a noble background. He was killed by his own soldiers during the siege of Aquileia.
bio|05-10|1774|Λουδοβίκος ΙΕ΄|Louis XV|Louis XV died in 1774 of smallpox. He was king of France from 1715 and was known for his mistresses and for France's defeat in the Seven Years' War.

bio|05-10|1849|Κατσουσίκα Χοκουσάι|Katsushika Hokusai|Katsushika Hokusai was a Japanese painter and printmaker of the ukiyo-e style. He became famous with the image "The Great Wave off Kanagawa" from the series "Thirty-Six Views of Mount Fuji".

bio|05-10|1878|Γκούσταβ Στρέζεμαν|Gustav Stresemann|Gustav Stresemann was a German politician. He was chancellor and foreign minister of the Weimar Republic and signed the Locarno Treaties in 1925. In 1926 he shared the Nobel Peace Prize.

bio|05-10|1886|Καρλ Μπαρτ|Karl Barth|Karl Barth was a Swiss Protestant theologian. He is considered one of the most important theologians of the 20th century. He wrote "The Epistle to the Romans" and "Church Dogmatics", and he opposed the Nazis.

bio|05-10|1889|Μιχαήλ Σαλτικόφ-Στσεντρίν|Mikhail Saltykov-Shchedrin|Mikhail Saltykov-Shchedrin was a Russian writer and satirist. He wrote the novel "The Golovlyov Family", a critique of Russian society and of the nobility.

bio|05-10|1899|Φρεντ Αστέρ|Fred Astaire|Fred Astaire was an American dancer and actor. He acted in musicals with Ginger Rogers, such as "Top Hat", and is regarded as one of the greatest dancers in film.
bio|05-10|1957|Σιντ Βίσιους|Sid Vicious|Sid Vicious was an English musician. He played bass for the Sex Pistols and became a symbol of punk. He died in 1979 of a drug overdose, at the age of 21.

bio|05-10|1969|Ντένις Μπέργκαμπ|Dennis Bergkamp|Dennis Bergkamp is a Dutch former footballer. He played for Ajax, Arsenal and the Netherlands national team. He is known for the way he controlled the ball and for his fear of flying.

bio|05-11|1871|Τζον Χέρσελ|John Herschel|John Herschel was an English astronomer and mathematician, the son of William Herschel. He observed the southern sky from the Cape of Good Hope, catalogued double stars and nebulae, and contributed to photography.

bio|05-11|1895|Τζίντου Κρισναμούρτι|Jiddu Krishnamurti|Jiddu Krishnamurti was an Indian thinker and speaker. He taught that truth is not found through organisations or teachers, but through personal observation. He dissolved the Order of the Star, which had been founded for him.

bio|05-11|1904|Σαλβαδόρ Νταλί|Salvador Dalí|Salvador Dalí was born in Figueres in Catalonia. He was a painter of Surrealism and painted "The Persistence of Memory" with its melting clocks. He was also an eccentric public figure.
bio|05-11|1916|Καμίλο Χοσέ Θέλα|Camilo José Cela|Camilo José Cela was a Spanish writer. He wrote the novel "The Family of Pascual Duarte". In 1989 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|05-11|1918|Ρίτσαρντ Φάινμαν|Richard Feynman|Richard Feynman was born in New York and was a physicist. He contributed to quantum electrodynamics, for which he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1965. He was also a popular teacher.

bio|05-11|1976|Άλβαρ Άαλτο|Alvar Aalto|Alvar Aalto died in Helsinki in 1976. He was a Finnish architect and designer, with buildings that use organic forms and natural materials, such as the Paimio Sanatorium.

bio|05-11|1981|Μπομπ Μάρλεϊ|Bob Marley|Bob Marley died in Miami in 1981 of cancer, at the age of 36. He was a Jamaican reggae musician who sang about peace and social justice, with songs such as "One Love" and "No Woman, No Cry".

bio|05-11|1984|Αντρές Ινιέστα|Andrés Iniesta|Andrés Iniesta is a Spanish former footballer. He played as a midfielder for Barcelona, and with Spain he scored the goal in the final of the 2010 World Cup. He also won two European Championships.

bio|05-11|2001|Ντάγκλας Άνταμς|Douglas Adams|Douglas Adams died in California in 2001, at the age of 49. He was an English science fiction writer and the creator of "The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy".

bio|05-12|454|Θεοδώριχος ο Μέγας|Theodoric the Great|Theodoric the Great was king of the Ostrogoths. He lived in Constantinople and became king of Italy in 493, with Ravenna as his capital. He ruled with relative peace and respect for the Romans.

bio|05-12|1820|Φλόρενς Νάιτινγκεϊλ|Florence Nightingale|Florence Nightingale was a British nurse. During the Crimean War she organised care for the wounded and improved hygiene in hospitals. She is regarded as the founder of modern nursing.

bio|05-12|1828|Ντάντε Γκάμπριελ Ροσέτι|Dante Gabriel Rossetti|Dante Gabriel Rossetti was born in London, the son of an Italian refugee. He was a poet and painter and founded the Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood. He painted works such as "Beata Beatrix".

bio|05-12|1884|Μπέντριχ Σμέτανα|Bedřich Smetana|Bedřich Smetana died in Prague in 1884, after years of deafness. He was a Czech composer and the founder of Czech national music, with works such as "The Bartered Bride" and "My Country".

bio|05-12|1907|Κάθριν Χέπμπορν|Katharine Hepburn|Katharine Hepburn was an American actress. She won four Academy Awards for Best Actress, a record that still stands, for films such as "Guess Who's Coming to Dinner" and "On Golden Pond". She was the partner of Spencer Tracy.

bio|05-12|1910|Ντόροθι Κρόουφουτ Χότζκιν|Dorothy Hodgkin|Dorothy Hodgkin was a British chemist. Using X-ray crystallography, she determined the structure of penicillin, vitamin B12 and insulin. In 1964 she was awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry.

bio|05-12|1935|Γιούζεφ Πιουσούτσκι|Józef Piłsudski|Józef Piłsudski was a Polish marshal and politician. He led Poland after its independence in 1918, defeated the Soviets in the Polish-Soviet War and governed in an authoritarian manner from 1926.

bio|05-12|1970|Νέλλυ Ζαχς|Nelly Sachs|Nelly Sachs was a German-Swedish poet and playwright of Jewish descent. She fled to Sweden in 1940 and wrote poetry about the suffering of the Holocaust. In 1966 she shared the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|05-12|2008|Ιρένα Σέντλερ|Irena Sendler|Irena Sendler was a Polish social worker. During the Nazi occupation she helped about 2,500 children escape from the Warsaw Ghetto. She died in 2008 at the age of 98.

bio|05-13|1717|Μαρία Θηρεσία|Maria Theresa|Maria Theresa was archduchess of Austria, queen of Hungary and Bohemia, and wife of the emperor. She ruled the Habsburg lands from 1740 to 1780 and was the mother of Marie Antoinette.

bio|05-13|1832|Ζορζ Κυβιέ|Georges Cuvier|Georges Cuvier was a French naturalist. He is regarded as the founder of comparative anatomy and palaeontology. He argued for the existence of extinct species, but rejected evolution.

bio|05-13|1907|Ντάφνι ντυ Μωριέ|Daphne du Maurier|Daphne du Maurier was a British writer. She wrote the novels "Rebecca" and "Jamaica Inn" and the short story "The Birds", which were adapted by Hitchcock.

bio|05-13|1930|Φρίντγιοφ Νάνσεν|Fridtjof Nansen|Fridtjof Nansen was a Norwegian explorer, scientist and diplomat. He led the "Fram" expedition to the Arctic and later helped refugees as High Commissioner. In 1922 he was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize.

bio|05-13|1950|Στίβι Γουόντερ|Stevie Wonder|Stevie Wonder is an American singer, multi-instrumentalist and songwriter. Blind from infancy, he became famous with the Motown label and with songs such as "Superstition" and "I Just Called to Say I Love You".

bio|05-13|1961|Γκάρι Κούπερ|Gary Cooper|Gary Cooper was an American actor. He won the Academy Award for Best Actor for the films "Sergeant York" and "High Noon". He was one of the great stars of Hollywood.
bio|05-13|1968|Σκοτ Μόρισον|Scott Morrison|Scott Morrison is an Australian politician of the Liberal Party. He was prime minister of Australia from 2018 to 2022.
bio|05-13|1986|Ρόμπερτ Πάτινσον|Robert Pattinson|Robert Pattinson is an English actor. He became known for the role of Edward Cullen in "Twilight" and as Bruce Wayne in "The Batman".

bio|05-13|2025|Χοσέ Μουχίκα|José Mujica|José Mujica was a Uruguayan politician. As a young man he was a member of the Tupamaros guerrilla group and was imprisoned for years. He was president of Uruguay from 2010 to 2015 and became known for his simple way of life.

bio|05-14|1610|Ερρίκος Δ΄|Henry IV|Henry IV was the first king of France from the House of Bourbon, from 1589. With the Edict of Nantes in 1598 he granted religious tolerance to the Protestants. He was assassinated in 1610 by a fanatical Catholic.

bio|05-14|1771|Ρόμπερτ Όουεν|Robert Owen|Robert Owen was a Welsh industrialist and social reformer, one of the first socialists. At the New Lanark mill he improved the conditions of the workers and founded schools. He also founded the community of New Harmony.

bio|05-14|1912|Άουγκουστ Στρίντμπεργκ|August Strindberg|August Strindberg died in Stockholm in 1912. He was a Swedish writer and playwright, a pioneer of naturalism and expressionism, with works such as "Miss Julie".

bio|05-14|1940|Έμμα Γκόλντμαν|Emma Goldman|Emma Goldman was born in Lithuania and emigrated to the United States. She was an anarchist, feminist and writer, known for her speeches on freedom and birth control. She was deported to Russia in 1919.

bio|05-14|1944|Τζορτζ Λούκας|George Lucas|George Lucas is an American director and producer. He created "Star Wars" and Indiana Jones, and he founded the companies Lucasfilm and Industrial Light & Magic.

bio|05-14|1953|Νοροντόμ Σιχαμόνι|Norodom Sihamoni|Norodom Sihamoni has been king of Cambodia since 2004, when his father Norodom Sihanouk resigned. Before that he was a dancer and diplomat and lived for years in Europe.

bio|05-14|1969|Κέιτ Μπλάνσετ|Cate Blanchett|Cate Blanchett is an Australian actress. She won two Oscars, one for Best Supporting Actress for "The Aviator" and one for Best Actress for "Blue Jasmine", and she also appeared in "The Lord of the Rings".

bio|05-14|1984|Μαρκ Ζάκερμπεργκ|Mark Zuckerberg|Mark Zuckerberg is an American businessman. In 2004, as a student at Harvard, he founded Facebook together with others. He is the head of Meta, which also includes Instagram and WhatsApp.

bio|05-14|1998|Φρανκ Σινάτρα|Frank Sinatra|Frank Sinatra was an American singer and actor. He was one of the greatest stars of the 20th century, with songs such as "My Way" and "New York, New York". He won the Oscar for Best Supporting Actor for the film "From Here to Eternity".

bio|05-15|1773|Κλέμενς φον Μέττερνιχ|Klemens von Metternich|Klemens von Metternich was an Austrian politician. He was Austria's foreign minister and the main architect of the Congress of Vienna in 1815. He opposed national and liberal movements, and also the Greek Revolution.

bio|05-15|1856|Λ. Φρανκ Μπάουμ|L. Frank Baum|L. Frank Baum was an American writer. He wrote the children's novel "The Wonderful Wizard of Oz" in 1900 and many more books about the land of Oz. The work was made into a film in 1939.

bio|05-15|1859|Πιερ Κιουρί|Pierre Curie|Pierre Curie was a French physicist. Together with his wife Marie he studied radioactivity, and in 1903 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics. He died in 1906 in a carriage accident.

bio|05-15|1886|Έμιλι Ντίκινσον|Emily Dickinson|Emily Dickinson was an American poet. She lived in isolation in Amherst, Massachusetts, and wrote almost 1,800 poems. Only a few were published while she was alive, and she was recognised after her death.

bio|05-15|1891|Μιχαήλ Μπουλγκάκοφ|Mikhail Bulgakov|Mikhail Bulgakov was born in Kyiv and became a Russian writer. He wrote the novel "The Master and Margarita", a satire of Soviet society, which was published after his death.
